behavior: _resolve_exec() prefers the A3 layout over an arbitrary PATH hit and returns the path through `current`, not a concrete versions/<v> dir, so the registered command survives an upgrade unrewritten (AC1).
A PATH hit that cannot start is not selected; resolution falls through to the module invocation rather than handing the supervisor a dead binary (AC2).
A healthy PATH hit is still selected when no layout exists — no regression for plain uv-tool installs (AC3) — and with neither layout nor PATH hit, `<python> -m hive.server` is returned (AC4).
The _executes probe answers False on any subprocess failure and never propagates, and a `current` pointing at a half-built version with no launcher inside does not win (AC5, AC6).
After `hive self-upgrade` on a machine with no prior install, `hive --version` works from a FRESH shell; an already-open shell is out of contract (AC7).
verification: manual: real non-admin Windows box. Every host-independent mechanism AC7 rests on — shim location, contents, dispatch through `current`, and the PATH write — is covered by f6-f9; what only hardware can answer is whether a new shell resolves it.

behavior: An upgrade repoints `current` and requires no launcher rewrite; launcher installation is idempotent, and repeated upgrades add no duplicate PATH entries (AC8).
Hive never writes to or deletes from ~/.local/bin — the boundary that rules out rejected option C (AC9).
A `hive*` on PATH that fails _executes() is reported and named alongside `dotf doctor --fix`, and is left unmodified; a healthy one and hive's own directory are not reported (AC10).
The hive bin dir is PREPENDED to the User PATH, not appended, so a stale ~/.local/bin entry does not win on ordering (AC11).
On POSIX the launcher install is an explicit no-op: ADR-019 is Windows-only, and a second unowned way to resolve `hive` must not appear on a platform where uv tool remains the install model.
